body.text: Exposed by real use of 'bonfyre-project foreign observe' on nine public housing surfaces. The organ decides http-versus-non-http and 2xx-versus-boundary, but it holds no notion of whether a fetch is permitted at all. Reddit's robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', so this epoch decided out-of-band never to fetch it and mined zero of its r/Dallas and r/arlington sublet and roommate supply; that decision lives only in this receipt, not in the machine, so the next carrier will re-derive or violate it. roomies.com is the inverse: robots.txt permits crawling and the origin still returned 403. Proposed capability, in the existing organ rather than a new one: a robots and rights preflight that emits a third observation_kind for 'not attempted, disallowed by source policy', so a policy exclusion is durably distinguishable from both a boundary denial and an absence of inventory. Until that exists, no atlas consumer can tell the three apart.

subject: ForeignTwin observer needs a rights-aware fetch policy, not just a transport
